newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen sees early settlement of Saudi border row.
newsitem.headline: Yemen sees early settlement of Saudi border row.

text.p: Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh said on Tuesday a final settlement of a 61-year-old border row with neighbouring Saudi Arabia was imminent.

"We will arrive at a final solution in the coming days or weeks," President Saleh told journalists accompanying Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef bin Abdul-Aziz who has been on an official visit to Yemen since Monday.
"The gap has been narrowed to a large extent and what remains is simple," Saleh said after a second round of talks with Prince Nayef.
An official earlier told Reuters Prince Nayef was expected to leave Yemen on Tuesday.

Yemen, one of the region's poorest countries, and oil-rich Saudi Arabia signed a memorandum of understanding in 1995 to resolve the border dispute. A joint committee looking into border demarcation has met scores of times since then, but its work is moving at a snail's pace, diplomats say.

Yemen has hinted in recent months it might resort to international arbitration. The two countries had several minor clashes in a border area potentially rich in oil and gas before they signed the memorandum.
